rendered: The document does not say that the authors chose a long melt step. It attributes long melt infiltration to other methods, which traditionally use it to ensure pore infiltration. The authors instead say their own vapor-based infiltration method is[1] significantly more scalable and less expensive[2] than those long melt routes. Their sulfur infiltration was run at a low temperature of[3] 175 °C[4], as an isothermal vapor phase process lasting[5] 1 h[6]. So the infiltration step in this work is short and low in temperature, not a multi-hour melt. The document gives no other reason for avoiding a long melt beyond the scalability and cost comparison.
